newsitem.title: USA: USDA halts imports of Dutch pork due swine fever.
newsitem.headline: USDA halts imports of Dutch pork due swine fever.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department said Tuesday it has halted imports of Dutch pork and pork products due to an outbreak of swine fever in the Netherlands.
A spokesman for USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service said any pork shipments already enroute would be stopped at the port of entry to be checked.

"The Netherlands is moving aggressively and doing all the right things," said APHIS spokesman Patrick Collins. "There's still concern at this point that the full dimension of the situation is an unknown, so as kind of an added precaution we've taken these measures."
He said it was "unclear at this point" when the policy might change.
Swine fever broke out in the North Brabant province of the southern Netherlands last week. Dutch authorities have started a massive pig cull to contain the fever.
The U.S. imported 10.7 million lbs of Dutch pork in 1995.
